findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1897 is the deprecated 'Cisco ACI Add-on for Splunk Enterprise' (TA_cisco-ACI), which collects APIC data via the API for the deprecated ACI app; it is not named 'Splunk Add-on for Cisco ACI' and nothing indicates it emits a cisco:nxos:syslog sourcetype for standalone NX-OS leaves.
findings.quote: **Splunk Add-on for Cisco ACI** ([Splunkbase 1897](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1897)) when **APIC**-adjacent **`cisco:nxos:syslog`** still lands beside standalone leaves
findings.suggested_fix: Drop 1897 (vendor says migrate to Cisco DC Networking, Splunkbase 7777) or name it correctly as deprecated; source NX-OS syslog from the actual syslog add-on/SC4S path and state the sourcetype that add-on really produces.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4241 is referenced in the cached catalogue as the 'VMware NSX-T Splunk App', not a Splunk-supported 'Splunk Add-on for VMware NSX'; the cached CIM-mapping NSX add-on is 'VMware NSX add-on' (TA-nsx, 6805). The same wrong name is repeated in detailedImplementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the actual NSX add-on/app being recommended and its correct Splunkbase ID after checking Splunkbase; update the detailedImplementation prerequisite paragraph to match.

findings.explanation: Network_Traffic models flow/firewall connection records (src, dest, bytes, action); VTEP peer state, VNI oper state and NVE encap/decap error counters are device health telemetry, not traffic sessions, and the Performance model covers host CPU/memory/storage/OS metrics. The SPL uses neither model and the 'schema' text justifying them is invented.
findings.suggested_fix: Set cimModels to [] (raw sourcetype search) or document that no CIM datamodel fits overlay tunnel health; remove the 'schema' and 'dataModelAcceleration' justifications that rely on these models.

findings.explanation: The category guide lists NX-OS syslog as `cisco:nexus:syslog`; `cisco:nxos:syslog` does not appear in the grounding sourcetype list, so readers following the guide will land data the search never reads.
findings.suggested_fix: Align on the sourcetype the deployed NX-OS syslog add-on/SC4S actually assigns (guide: cisco:nexus:syslog) or explain the rename.

findings.explanation: The SPL copy inside the fenced spl block has markdown bold markers (**...**) injected into field names and commands (`**eventstats perc90**`, `lookup **fabric_site_pod_map**`), so a reader pasting it gets a syntax error. Step 2 also tells readers to wrap the index union in `%evpn_vxlan_tunnel_idx%`, but Splunk macros are invoked with backticks.
findings.suggested_fix: Paste the SPL verbatim without emphasis markers and write the macro as `evpn_vxlan_tunnel_idx` in backticks.

findings.explanation: evidence names the saved search operations_evpn_vxlan_tunnel_health while implementation and detailedImplementation name uc_18_3_11_overlay_health_core / uc_18_3_11_overlay_health_alert; detailedImplementation also says to schedule over earliest=-70m while the SPL hardcodes earliest=-4h@m.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one saved-search name across fields and state the alert time range consistently with the SPL (or note the override).

findings.explanation: UC-18.3.4 is 'VXLAN Tunnel and Overlay Health: VTEP Reachability, BGP-EVPN Convergence...', a near-duplicate of this UC, not a MAC-mobility UC; the closely overlapping siblings UC-18.3.9 and UC-18.3.16 (VTEP reachability) are not mentioned at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite only UC-18.3.5 for MAC mobility and explicitly delineate this UC from UC-18.3.4, UC-18.3.9 and UC-18.3.16.

findings.explanation: The URL is the Cisco.com home page, not the configuration guide named in the title, so the citation cannot be followed.
findings.quote:
"title": "Cisco Nexus 9000 NX-OS VXLAN BGP EVPN Configuration Guide",
      "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the actual Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS VXLAN Configuration Guide page for the referenced release.

findings.explanation: It is not clear that `show nve interface` / `show nve vni` output on NX-OS carries encap/decap error counters; on many trains these come from `show interface nve1 counters` or per-peer/VNI counter commands.
findings.quote: **`sourcetype=nxos:nve_counters`** ( **`show nve interface`** / **`show nve vni`** counter exports with **`encap_errors`**, **`decap_errors`**)
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Nexus 9000 VXLAN configuration/command reference for the command that exposes encap/decap error counters and name it, along with whether the counters are cumulative.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by an automated agent reviewer, with no SME sign-off, while containing wrong add-on names and an SPL that drops most of its own lanes.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/unverified until a human SME has validated the SPL against real NX-OS/EOS data.

findings.explanation: Nothing in the UC involves Hyper-V; the hypervisor correlation discussed is VMware vMotion/NSX.
Splunkbase 1546 is listed as 'REST API Modular Input' (rest_ta), a third-party app, not a Splunk-branded add-on.
findings.suggested_fix: Call it 'REST API Modular Input (rest_ta, Splunkbase 1546)'.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `stats ... BY _time leaf peer_ip vni_key` drops every event where a BY field is null. vni_key is `tonumber(coalesce(...,""))`, which is null whenever no VNI field exists, so network:bgp_neighbor rows (bgp_bad), cisco:nxos:syslog rows (syslog_nve_hit) and interface-level nxos:nve_counters rows never reach the output; the advertised control-plane and syslog lanes are dead. Use fillnull or coalesce vni_key to a sentinel before stats.

counter_bad fires whenever encap_errors/decap_errors is >0, and stats sums the raw values per 5m bin. If the NX-OS/EOS counters are cumulative (as `show` output normally is), any leaf with a historical non-zero counter alerts forever and encap_errors_total inflates with poll count; a delta (streamstats/latest-earliest per peer) is needed. Verify counter semantics per platform.
After `bin _time span=5m`, `earliest(_time)`/`latest(_time)` return the bin start, so first_seen and last_seen are always equal; compute them before bin or from a copied raw timestamp.

summary: The detection idea (fusing NVE peer state, VNI state, EVPN BGP state and encap/decap counters) is sound and the troubleshooting prose is useful, but the SPL silently drops most lanes at the stats BY clause, the add-on list mis-names or mis-describes Splunkbase 1897 and 4241, the CIM mapping does not fit, and several reference/implementation details are placeholders or inconsistent.
